# Run briefs

Two kinds of brief exist, and they come from different places.

**Generated by `bin/new-run`, never copied from here:** the solver brief (`--role solver`), with its fixed sections
(Gates, Frozen before running, Classes every start ends in, Budget, Kill criteria, Cycle exit criteria, the
embedded claims schema), and the two referee briefs (`--role referee --question certify|hypotheses`). The tool
embeds the schema and the rules text so that the least mechanical step has the same skeleton every time, and
`bin/lint-brief` checks the filled brief against `SCHEMAS.md` before the user's gate.

**Copied from here, over the `--role other` skeleton `bin/new-run` makes, then filled:**

| template | for | worker |
|---|---|---|
| `canary-BRIEF.md` | the context and sandbox canary: one per route the instance enables, before real work on that route, and after any change to the hook, the settings, an agent definition or a harness note | yes — the canary *is* the worker |
| `setup-audit-BRIEF.md` | an outside audit of a solver run's set-up before it is launched | yes — an outside model, sandboxed |
| `outside-reader-BRIEF.md` | one stuck question, packeted for a party with no stake | yes — an outside model, sandboxed |
| `handoff-audit-BRIEF.md` | a fidelity check of a handoff against the record | yes — an outside model, sandboxed |
| `PROVENANCE.md` | the record of any run whose result is not a claim: an audit, a packet, a restatement on byte copies, an outside run the user launched | no — written by the orchestrator after the run |
| `restatement-BRIEF.md` | a claim restated with the wording its artifact certifies, the artifact unchanged (the source's run 205) | no — the orchestrator assembles it |
| `repair-BRIEF.md` | the task sections of a solver run that repairs a check a referee found wider than what it certifies (the source's run 304), pasted over `--role solver`'s slots | yes — a solver |

A run with no worker that makes a claim (a restatement on byte copies of its artifact) is a `--role other` run holding the
byte copies under `output/`, where the claim's artifact must be, with `RUN/.source-run` and a `PROVENANCE.md`; it is refereed
like any other. A record of an outside run holds its copies under `input/`.

Every brief says, in its own words, what the worker will and will not see, and the packet lists every file. A
record file (`BRIEF.md`, `CLAIMS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `RULES.md`, …) copied into a packet goes under another name;
`bin/verify-data` refuses the original names inside a run's `input/`.
